notes.title: Hottest update yet
notes.content:
Hey, how's life going? Today I'm bringing you a brand new update to Side Effect. It's about challenges! There are 3 challenges so far which you can try to beat:
[olist]
[*] [b]Long Shot[/b] is about scoring garbage to recycler's yellow ring from the greatest distance possible.
[*] [b]Fast Collector[/b] is about collecting as much garbage as you can in 2 minutes.
[*] [b]Floor is Lava[/b] is about escaping lava and the shortest time wins.
[/olist]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39863452/ae1cae80e14c8cbc17695eae661645a562a68b92.png[/img]

Each challenge record score is synchronized with the database which means as soon as you achieve a new record, everyone will instantly know!

[b]Apart from this huge feature here are other things included in this 0.3.2 update:[/b]
[list]
[*] Added three challenges which check for internet connection and sync with database
[*] Patreon support message has been added at the end of credits screen
[*] "Support & get rewarded" button added to the main menu
[*] Main menu cleaned up from unnecessary buttons
[*] Falling down the cliff now correctly resets current scene again
[*] Recycler under the hood code optimizations
[*] Renamed "Options" to "Settings"
[/list]
Personally my favourite challenge is the Long Shot where I scored 83.37 metres so far. Give them a shot and tell me your favourite. Here's video of my personal record:

[previewyoutube=jBA4vG33BXw;full][/previewyoutube]
For now that's all from me, have an awesome day.

[b]Sincerely, your dev[/b]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/3Cz73Nt.png[/img]

notes.title: Smol but still an update
notes.content:
Yo, it's me again guess what I have for you... a new update! It's 0.2.1 and for this update I was wondering why the "Report an Issue" form was empty for the entire month. Not sure if my programming skills are so on point or players just don't care to report problems when they see them (I thinks it's the second option but not sure).

Anyways here's what I got for ya:

[olist]
[*] Garbage is now randomly tinted by dirty color to make them look more older and damaged.

[*] Fox now collects garbage around itself automatically without waiting for the player. This is compensated however by decreased "garbage visibility range" from 20 metres to 10 for Tobi.

[*] "COMMING SOON" message typo in main menu corrected.

[*] Fox now checks for valid paths before he moves which should rule out any possible "him getting stuck" situations.

[*] Facebook button and group removed.

[*] Recycler's salvo progress bar has now an icon.

[*] Recycler also shows small hotkey hint about how to respawn it for those players who might be confused or just didn't pay too much attention during "tutorial" section of gameplay.

[*] Updated look of golden garbage to make it look more distinct since sometimes new players are not aware that this is a collectable.

[*] Changed butterfly's path so that now it will show the player more of the forest and navigates him straight to the next stage.

[*] Butterfly has been sped up to match player's speed now.

[*] Golden garbage has been excluded from total garbage counter which is displayed on credits screen.

[*] Player's speed now changes when he meets fox.

[*] Increased player's speed during gameplay from 4 to 5.

[*] Fixed an issue where total collected garbage number wouldn't calculate properly on credits screen.

[*] Sad music has been shortened a little to prevent music clashing / cutting when you progress from first to second stage.
[/olist]

I really hope these tweaks, fixes and additions will make your gameplay experience even more interesting and as always if you encounter something weird in the game or you break it somehow, please let me know by filling up the issue form from the main menu. I will be very grateful for that.

That's all from me guys, have a wonderful day.

[b]Sincerely, your dev[/b]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/3Cz73Nt.png[/img]

notes.title: 🦊 Tobi's update 0.1.3 is out!
notes.content:
Yo guys, many players have experienced Tobi getting stuck during the gameplay. This is very unpleasant situation since Tobi is essential for the story to continue and with him being stuck in one place forever the player won't be able to finish the demo.

Apart from this main problem I've decided to add and tweak more features of the game, some are smaller others are larger, to make it more interesting for you guys.

[b]Here is the list of changes / fixes for 0.1.3:[/b]

[olist]
[*] When bringing garbage to recycler, Tobi will now select proper 'NavMesh' position on the ground which will make sure he will not get stuck anymore.

[*] I have flattened bumpy terrain under the small downhill river to prevent players getting accidentally stuck while walking in the river.

[*] Tobi's monologue speech has been simplified to communicate story more clearly.

[*] Sometimes Tobi would not pick up garbage when player recycles, even though there's clearly trash near him. This is also fixed.

[*] Garbage will no longer sink underwater but will now float on the surface surface, which will make it easier for you to find it.

[*] Tobi's garbage collection mechanics explaining has been simplified since before it took quite long time for him to explain it.

[*] 1 golden trash has been moved to apparent location to make it more clear for the player that there are collectables in the demo.

[*] A flower pot can now be removed & recycled from Tobi's dead child's head to reveal an ugly truth (yes I know).

[*] When you fall to your death, game will now respawn you inside the cave instead of going back to the main menu.

[*] Tobi's range at which he asks player to follow him has been decreased a little to make it more natural.

[*] Facebook and Youtube social media buttons have been hidden from the main menu to prevent visual clutter.

[*] Tobi's crying sequence has been shortened a bit.

[*] Increased size of garbage collector's surface to make it easier to hit it with trash from greater distances.
[/olist]

A huge thank you to all players who saw an issue in the game and decided to report it via a form online, I'm grateful for that. That's all for this update, I hope you will give it a try and let me know how you like these new changes.

[b]Sincerely, your dev[/b]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/3Cz73Nt.png[/img]

notes.title: 🦊 Tobi's learning to speak
notes.content:
[h1]Communication by symbols[/h1]
[h2]Symbols, pictograms or emojis?[/h2]
Many games communicate ideas to you by words. English, German, Italian or Slovak, doesn't matter they are still words which need to be translated if the game wants to have broader player base. Symbols (pictograms or emojis) however are a universal language. They can be "read" instantly and when put together one after the other they can form simple sentences. That's why I decided to have such a communication system in the game.

[h2]Complexity from simplicity[/h2]
I design every single emoji to be as simple and as straight forward as possible so that it is easy and fast to understand. When these simple emojis are placed in sequence one after the other with defined set of simple sentence rules, they can communicate more complex ideas.

Just take a look on this video and try it for yourself if you can understand what this fox is saying:

[previewyoutube=q5TVs3UhSs0;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Artstyle & Graphics
notes.content:
Many people have asked me how I achieved this style of graphics and after giving them a brief 2-3 lines of overly simplified explanation, I finally decided to write detailed article on how Side Effect rendering actually works under the hood.

Understanding this process requires some technical knowledge about rendering, just sayin'..

[h1]Dissecting a Frame[/h1]
Let's talk about how the frame is rendered step by step. There are 3 features which play together:
[olist]
[*] Unlit geometry
[*] Edge detection
[*] Background fog
[/olist]
All objects are rendered using unlit shader (1) and then custom post processing effect is rendered on top (2 & 3), giving it the final look.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39863452/6ae65b18d0b70b5f3c80e2798987fe8e968fcfa4.png[/img]

[h2]Lighting[/h2]
First of all, Side Effect doesn't use any lights or shadows which means I can save some performance by not doing any lighting calculations. Toon shading also isn't part of rendering since that requires a light to be present.

This means every object in the frame is rendered as a opaque or alpha clipped geometry using unlit shader. Here is how the unlit frame looks like before post processing:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39863452/695b220611cd3cd4098fbf692ecf9eb37135b84c.png[/img]

After this step a custom post processing effect is executed which combines unlit frame, edge detection and distance based fog together.

[h2]Background Texture[/h2]
If you look reeally close you will see that orange background fog has some faint texture overlaid on top of it. This is because a simple orange color looked too boring to me so I added this texture overlay to make it more alive, here it is:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39863452/b2d55b5e2cc2a69f4282dd01c68e57da168b9d20.png[/img]

This texture needs to be tileable (seamless) so that it can be repeated indefinitely. Now I can decrease intensity of its darker parts using power function and tint it orange like his:

[b][i]float4 b = pow(OVERLAY_TEX, 0.4) * _OrangeColor;[/i][/b]

Remember this "b" variable we will need it later. Last step is to tile this texture across entire screen which looks like this:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39863452/0273b4febaf9f5aeb83f454b1331eef487b606c6.png[/img]

[h2]Depth Texture[/h2]
Since every opaque / alpha clipped geometry writes depth data into a depth buffer, I can retrieve this information using a depth texture from the main camera. Here is how the depth texture looks like, darker the pixel is the closer it is to the camera and vice versa:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39863452/91317ac72faae156e49921a375ce7c60001a215a.png[/img]

Looks pretty foggy already doesn't it? I will use this fog gradient later. So why is this depth texture necessary you ask?

[h2]Edge Detection[/h2]
To draw edges around objects I use depth based [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberts_cross]Roberts Cross operator[/url]. Instead of feeding it frame buffer color data I feed it camera's depth texture to calculate outline around objects. I've set its settings so that even slightest change in depth results in faint color gradient. 

This may seem like there is fresnel (rim light) effect added as well while in reality it's just depth based edge detection on its own. You can see this in action especially well on the right side where path goes downward. Here is how frame looks like after edge detection is calculated on it:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39863452/e8a3e783f86a799bcd8008cedb533fb37e0b1129.png[/img]

If I now take this edge detected texture, tint it orange and add that result on top of the original frame, 

[b][i]float4 a = ORIGINAL_FRAME + edge * _OrangeColor;[/i][/b]

this is what I get:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39863452/1e13021b9aca1b8100f71d90dff62ee0d14aa821.png[/img]

This image just showcases how would it looked like before fog was added.

[h2]Final Image[/h2]
Still remember that "b" variable? Let's combine it with "a" variable (really creative names I know) from before to get the final image:

[b][i]float4 final = lerp(a, b, FOG_FACTOR);[/i][/b]

This final formula linearly interpolates from "a" to "b" based on FOG_FACTOR interpolant. FOG_FACTOR is nothing more than just raw sample taken from depth texture.

Put simply, take a look at the depth texture from above, again. Lerp function here will make sure all white parts of the texture will be rendered using "b" variable (which contains orange tileable background) and all black parts will be rendered using "a" variable (which contains orange edges applied on top of the original frame). 

Everything between black and white will be linearly interpolated between those two values.

[h1]FAQ[/h1]
[olist]
[*] [b]What engine / rendering API are you using?[/b]
I'm using Unity Engine for this project, but I wrote this article without using any Unity specific features so that anyone can implement this style of graphics in any engine or rendering API.

[*] [b]Who is that cute foxy thing?[/b]
His name is Tobi and you can find more of him on any Side Effect's social media, official website or in the game of course once it gets released.
[/olist]
I hope this gave you a better understanding of the rendering process that Side Effect uses. Feel free to ask any questions below.

notes.title: Core game mechanics finally polished
notes.content:
There was a long time question of how you as a player will be able to get rid of all that garbage laying around to make progress in the game. This core mechanics now gives you ability to pick any garbage object from the ground and manipulate with it. Recycler will also become handy.

[h2]But how does it work exactly? [/h2]
First of all you need to find garbage and spawn a recycler near it. Then by holding the left mouse button (LMB for short) will you be able to pick up the garbage. After that pressing right mouse button will throw garbage forward. Garbage will fly in direction you're facing so make sure you aim at the recycler's catcher so that it can catch it.

[h2]What is Recycler?[/h2]
Recycler is a key machine to successful garbage recycling in the game and it also keeps track of how many garbage pieces have you recycled already. 

Recycler has a big circle on top of it called "The Garbage Catcher". Whatever garbage touches this circle will be recycled and counted. This means you can throw garbage from far away towards the catcher and hope it hits it. Less courageous players can walk up to it while holding garbage and still get recycling done!



[previewyoutube=F0VFp74XxAA;full][/previewyoutube]
